sources.label: HTML Standard §popover attribute (the attribute whose hint value this page's change modifies)
whatwg/html PR #12345 — Simplify popover=hint behaviours & related spec fixes

inventory.name: popover="hint" attribute — revised stacking and closing model

syntax.rationale: The declaration surface the page documents is the popover attribute's value grammar, spelled in this section's table as the three enumerated states popover="auto", popover="hint" and popover="manual" (each rendered as <code> in the first column). The feature adds no new attribute, interface or IDL: it is a behaviour change to the existing popover="hint" value, so the grammar in the background table is the whole surface. The only developer-visible control beyond the attribute values is the enablement flag in the at-a-glance table, covered under context and recorded as a divergence in notes.

inputs.rationale: The inputs are the concrete attribute assignments a developer writes, shown in the worked example: popovertarget="menu" and popovertarget="tip" on the two trigger buttons, and popover="auto" / popover="hint" on the two popover elements. The revised model changes no argument or value — the only inputs are these HTML attributes, defined by the HTML Standard's popover attribute and left unchanged by PR #12345.

outputs.rationale: The observable outputs are the revised stacking and closing behaviours the #what-changed table states: a hint always renders above auto popovers in the top layer, opening a hint never closes an open auto, opening a new hint closes the previous hint, and light-dismiss on outside click is unchanged. These are top-layer/rendering state transitions rather than a script return value.

errors.rationale: The page documents no error or exception path: no throwing surface, no InvalidStateError and no failure mode appear anywhere in its prose or tables. The cited sources do describe an error path the page omits (PR #12345's commit message and the ChromeStatus summary both state that showing a popover during another popover's show/hide is no longer allowed and throws InvalidStateError), so this is a recorded coverage gap, not a claim that no error surface exists.

context.rationale: The at-a-glance table fixes the exposure context: 'Status in 149: In developer trial (behind a flag)', 'Ships by default: Chrome 150', the enablement flag, 'Standards position: Firefox: Positive · Safari: Positive', and the ChromeStatus record. The live record corroborates the Firefox and Safari 'Positive' views and, via its dev-trial stage (desktop_first/android_first 149) and ship stage (desktop_first 150), the 149-trial / 150-default timeline; its summary status 'Proposed' and its no-flag gating diverge from the page's flag instruction — both recorded in notes, neither adjudicated.

lifecycle.rationale: The #what-changed section states the state transitions with nothing to construct or tear down in script: a hint is shown above autos, opening a hint never closes an open auto, opening a new hint closes the previously-open hint (tooltip-style replacement), and clicking outside closes light-dismissable popovers. The PR commit message lists the same transitions ('Showing a hint popover doesn't hide auto popovers', 'Showing a hint popover hides non-parent hint popovers', 'Clicking outside popovers consistently hides them').

examples.rationale: The page's single complete <pre><code> example: a button opens an auto popover menu, a button inside it targets a sibling hint popover, and the following prose states that in Chrome 149+ showing the hint no longer dismisses the menu and that dismissing the hint leaves the auto open. Every attribute used (popovertarget, popover="auto", popover="hint") is defined by the linked HTML Standard popover attribute.

compatibility.rationale: The browser-support table lists Chrome '149 — revised model', Edge '149 (Chromium)', Firefox 'Positive signal; implementation tracking' and Safari 'Positive signal; implementation tracking'. The live record's Firefox and Safari views both read 'Positive' (matching the 'Positive' half of each cell); 'implementation tracking' has no counterpart field in the record, and '149 — revised model' is corroborated only by the record's 149 dev-trial stage — both nuances recorded in notes, neither adjudicated.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page documents no security or privacy surface: the change affects only top-layer stacking and light-dismiss behaviour, adding no permission, origin, storage, network or script-readable surface, and the page carries no security or privacy sentence. The live record's security_review_status and privacy_review_status are both 'Pending' (fetched 2026-10-07), so this is a recorded coverage gap rather than a clean absolution.

NOT ADJUDICATED HERE. COVERAGE GAPS, NOT CONTRADICTIONS (the page omits what the cited sources state, but says nothing that contradicts them): the PR and the record summary both add (a) nesting an auto popover inside a hint popover now downgrades the auto to behave as a hint, (b) showing a popover during another popover's show/hide is no longer allowed and throws InvalidStateError, and (c) hiding an auto popover does not hide unrelated hint popovers — none of these appear on the page. UNSOURCED PAGE SPECIFICS, not contradicted but not corroborated by any linked source: the 'Hints sit above autos ... not interleaved' stacking phrasing (the PR commit message describes hiding semantics, not painting order; the current spec's two-list model — showing auto popover list and showing hint popover list — is consistent with 'not interleaved' but the page's exact 'above' wording was not found as a literal sentence), the Firefox/Safari 'implementation tracking' qualifier (the record's views say only 'Positive'), and the compatibility section's workaround 'double-closes' prose.
